title: The Transformer
tagline: Self-attention, multi-head attention, positional encodings, the Transformer block and its variants
summary: Since 2017 the Transformer has been the architecture of language models. This course derives self-attention and multi-head attention, positional encodings, the residual Transformer block, the encoder, decoder and encoder–decoder variants, the cost of attention, and the efficient and sparse variants used at scale.

chapters.title: Self-attention
chapters.summary: Queries, keys and values, scaled dot-product attention and attention as a weighted average.

chapters.title: Multi-head attention
chapters.summary: Heads and projections, causal masking and the shapes of attention computations.

chapters.title: Positional information
chapters.summary: Sinusoidal and learned position embeddings, relative positions, RoPE and ALiBi.

chapters.title: The Transformer block
chapters.summary: The residual stream, layer normalisation and RMSNorm, feed-forward layers and gated activations such as SwiGLU.

chapters.title: Encoders, decoders and encoder–decoders
chapters.summary: BERT-style encoders, GPT-style decoders and T5-style encoder–decoders, and what each is good for.

chapters.title: The cost of attention
chapters.summary: Quadratic cost in sequence length, memory traffic and FlashAttention.

chapters.title: Efficient and long-context attention
chapters.summary: Sparse, sliding-window and linear attention, and multi-query and grouped-query attention.

chapters.title: Mixture of experts
chapters.summary: Sparse expert layers, routing, load balancing and the trade-offs of conditional computation.
